title: His violin from France and the Stradivarius label
summary: He still has a violin brought from France; Russell explains the label means a Stradivari model, not an original.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: I'm glad I learned it. Have you ever played it recently, the violin? No, not here lately.
No, you know, many years since I played. Well, playing the beat so long, I guess my fingers got too big for it, you know. And, I got the violin in there now. And Bill told me, see the Stradivari.
I remember you showed it to me, you got that in France, you said, right?
Yeah, I brought that from France when I was over there playing.
I think the label says made in Germany on it too.
I think so. I think it does.
There couldn't be real Stradivari's, they were made in Italy.
Well, where they was making the Stradivari's, Bill?
They were made in Italy, up in Northern Italy. Is that right? A little town called Cremona. Up near Milan, and near Florence, and Venice, up in between those towns, up there.
They all was made right then in Italy. In Italy. Did you ever get any? Well, Germany and France didn't make that.

No, they made a lot of violins in Germany, though more than any place really in Germany. Well, why did they have Stradivari's? Oh, it means it's that model. It was made to look like that. Made like, made the same modern, the model or the pattern, the same pattern like the Stradivari's. Did you get to Italy during the war? Yes, I went, we was in Italy, in the Tini. You went to Italy?
